description: Three-premise conditional incompatibility, with the grades observation making the population boundary explicit. Separate closed Bool/Nat/Empty deletion-control obligations are included; automatic registry-computed minimality is not claimed. The grades observation supplies one member a of the shared Being carrier; it is used only for this population fact. Unbounded degree extension at esse gives a being b more such than a. The existing grades-to-maximum principle at esse then supplies a maximal being m, and extension at m supplies a being more such than m, contradicting its maximality. The three explicit premises therefore cannot coexist. No homogeneous scale, preorder, totality, genus principle, causal-ascent premise, causal relation, or excluded middle is used; MoreIn remains the shared primitive comparative. This connects the degree fork's unbounded branch to an existing root-path maximum-existence assumption without establishing either side or selecting a preferred member for rejection. The stronger two-premise boundary is that the maximum principle and unbounded extension admit no member of Being; observed grades rule out that empty-carrier case. Supplementary closed Comparator obligations separately witness every single deletion: the same finite Bool interpretation satisfies maximum and grades while extension fails; the same infinite Nat interpretation satisfies grades and extension while the maximum principle fails; the same Empty-carrier interpretation satisfies both universal principles vacuously while grades fail. Nat and Empty are not represented as nonempty finite-registry witnesses, so automatic registered inclusion-minimality remains unavailable. These are formal omission controls, not metaphysical emptiness, source attribution of a new rival, or truth of a premise. No root premise changes. Axiom inspection reports no axioms for incompatible, withoutUnbounded and withoutGrades; withoutMaximumPrinciple uses exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound through the existing Nat model proof. The Comparator profile permits those three axioms for the combined obligations.
